body_html:
How to think about it

  • 1 minute = 60 seconds; 1 hour = 60 minutes.
  • Add 12 to p.m. hours for the 24-hour clock: 7:20 p.m. → 19:20.
  • Find a duration by counting on to the next hour, then on.

Examples

Example

Ravi ran 100 m in 1 minute 5 seconds. How many seconds?

60 + 5

Answer: 65 seconds

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Using 100 seconds in a minuteThere are 60 seconds in a minute.
Writing 2 p.m. as 2:00 in 24-hour timeIt is 14:00.

faq.q: How many seconds are in an hour?

items.e: The hour hand is between 5 and 6, so the hour is still 5. The minute hand points to 4: 4 × 5 = 20 minutes past. Times from midnight to midday are am. So it is 5:20 am.
The hour hand is between 2 and 3, so the hour is still 2. The minute hand points to 6: 6 × 5 = 30 minutes past. Times from midnight to midday are am. So it is 2:30 am.

The hour hand is between 12 and 1, so the hour is still 12. The minute hand points to 9: 9 × 5 = 45 minutes past. Just after midnight is the start of the morning, so it is am: 12 am, not 12 pm. So it is 12:45 am.
The hour hand is between 5 and 6, so the hour is still 5. The minute hand points to 6: 6 × 5 = 30 minutes past. Times from midday to midnight are pm. So it is 5:30 pm.

The hour hand is between 8 and 9, so the hour is still 8. The minute hand is 3 small marks past the 10. Count in 5s to 50, then on in 1s: 53 minutes past. Times from midnight to midday are am. So it is 8:53 am.

The hour hand is between 3 and 4, so the hour is still 3. The minute hand is 1 small mark past the 7. Count in 5s to 35, then on in 1s: 36 minutes past. Times from midday to midnight are pm. So it is 3:36 pm.

The hour hand is between 12 and 1, so the hour is still 12. The minute hand is 1 small mark past the 4. Count in 5s to 20, then on in 1s: 21 minutes past. Just after midday is the afternoon, so it is pm: 12 pm, not 12 am. So it is 12:21 pm.

items.q: Write 17 minutes to 4 in the afternoon as a 12-hour digital time.
items.e: “17 minutes to 4” means 17 minutes before 4 o’clock. 60 − 17 = 43, so it is 3:43. In the afternoon is pm, so it is 3:43 pm.

items.q: Write 22 minutes to 9 in the morning as a 12-hour digital time.
items.e: “22 minutes to 9” means 22 minutes before 9 o’clock. 60 − 22 = 38, so it is 8:38. In the morning is am, so it is 8:38 am.

items.q: Write 12 minutes past 7 in the evening as a 12-hour digital time.
items.e: “12 minutes past 7” means 12 minutes after 7 o’clock: 7:12. In the evening is pm, so it is 7:12 pm.

items.q: Write 8 minutes to 12 in the morning as a 12-hour digital time.
items.e: “8 minutes to 12” means 8 minutes before 12 o’clock. 60 − 8 = 52, so it is 11:52. In the morning is am, so it is 11:52 am.
The hour hand is between 8 and 9, so the hour is still 8. The minute hand points to 10: 10 × 5 = 50 minutes past. Times from midnight to midday are am. So it is 8:50 am.
The hour hand is between 5 and 6, so the hour is still 5. The minute hand points to 7: 7 × 5 = 35 minutes past. Times from midday to midnight are pm. So it is 5:35 pm.
pm times are after midday. Add 12 to the hour: 5 + 12 = 17. So 5:10 pm is 17:10. (Do not just put a 1 in front: 15:10 is 3:10 pm.)
pm times are after midday. Add 12 to the hour: 1 + 12 = 13. So 1:15 pm is 13:15. (Do not just put a 1 in front: 11:15 is 11:15 am.)
am times are before midday, so the hour stays the same. A 24-hour time always has 4 digits, so put a 0 in front of a 1-digit hour: 7:40 am is 07:40.
am times are before midday, so the hour stays the same. A 24-hour time always has 4 digits, so put a 0 in front of a 1-digit hour: 8:10 am is 08:10.
pm times are after midday. Add 12 to the hour: 9 + 12 = 21. So 9:10 pm is 21:10. (Do not just put a 1 in front: 19:10 is 7:10 pm.)
pm times are after midday. Add 12 to the hour: 11 + 12 = 23. So 11:30 pm is 23:30.
am times are before midday, so the hour stays the same. Do not add 12. 11:40 am is 11:40.
12 am is the hour just after midnight. In 24-hour time a new day starts at 00:00, so 12:30 am is 00:30.
pm times are after midday. Add 12 to the hour: 3 + 12 = 15. So 3:43 pm is 15:43. (Do not just put a 1 in front: 13:43 is 1:43 pm.)
pm times are after midday. Add 12 to the hour: 2 + 12 = 14. So 2:06 pm is 14:06. (Do not just put a 1 in front: 12:06 is 12:06 pm.)
Hours from 13 to 23 are p.m. times. Take away 12: 16 − 12 = 4. So 16:35 is 4:35 p.m. (Not 6:35 p.m.: do not just drop the 1. 16 − 12 = 4, not 6.)
p.m. times are after noon. Add 12 to the hour: 9 + 12 = 21. So 9:20 p.m. is 21:20. (09:20 is in the morning.)
00 is the hour just after midnight. In 12-hour time that hour is 12 a.m. So 00:45 is 12:45 a.m., 45 minutes after midnight. (12:45 p.m. is 45 minutes after noon.)

items.q: A ferry sails from 09:40 to 11:15. How long is the trip?
items.e: Count on in jumps: 09:40 to 10:00 is 20 minutes; 10:00 to 11:00 is 1 hour; 11:00 to 11:15 is 15 minutes. 1 hour + 20 minutes + 15 minutes = 1 hour 35 minutes. (Not 1 hour 75 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the clock numbers.)

items.q: A football tournament runs from 13:25 to 16:10. How long does it run?
items.e: Count on in jumps: 13:25 to 14:00 is 35 minutes; 14:00 to 16:00 is 2 hours; 16:00 to 16:10 is 10 minutes. 2 hours + 35 minutes + 10 minutes = 2 hours 45 minutes. (Not 2 hours 85 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the clock numbers.)

items.q: A ferry leaves at 14:35. The trip takes 2 hours 50 minutes. What time does it arrive?
items.e: Add 2 hours: 14:35 → 16:35. Then add 50 minutes: 25 minutes takes you to 17:00, and 25 minutes more is 17:25.

items.q: A ferry arrives at 13:10 after a trip of 2 hours 25 minutes. What time did it leave?
items.e: Count back 2 hours: 13:10 → 11:10. Then count back 25 minutes: 10 minutes takes you to 11:00, and 15 minutes more is 10:45. (Count back to find a start time. Adding gives a time after 13:10.)

items.q: A train leaves at 08:35 and arrives at 15:20. How long is the trip?
items.e: Count on in jumps: 08:35 to 09:00 is 25 minutes; 09:00 to 15:00 is 6 hours; 15:00 to 15:20 is 20 minutes. 6 hours + 25 minutes + 20 minutes = 6 hours 45 minutes. (Not 6 hours 85 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the clock numbers.)

items.q: A hockey game on TV is on from 17:48 to 20:30. How long is it on?
items.e: Count on in jumps: 17:48 to 18:00 is 12 minutes; 18:00 to 20:00 is 2 hours; 20:00 to 20:30 is 30 minutes. 2 hours + 12 minutes + 30 minutes = 2 hours 42 minutes. (Not 2 hours 82 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the clock numbers.)

items.q: A concert starts at 19:40 and lasts 3 hours 35 minutes. What time does it end?
items.e: Add 3 hours: 19:40 → 22:40. Then add 35 minutes: 20 minutes takes you to 23:00, and 15 minutes more is 23:15.
Hours 13 to 23 are pm. Take away 12: 15 − 12 = 3. So 15:55 is 3:55 pm. (Do not just drop the 1: 5:55 pm is 17:55.)
The hour 08 is less than 12, so it is a morning time: am. Drop the 0 at the front: 8:15 am.
The hour 09 is less than 12, so it is a morning time: am. Drop the 0 at the front: 9:15 am.
Hours 13 to 23 are pm. Take away 12: 21 − 12 = 9. So 21:55 is 9:55 pm. (Take away 12, not 10: 11:55 pm is 23:55.)
Hours 13 to 23 are pm. Take away 12: 22 − 12 = 10. So 22:05 is 10:05 pm. (Take away 12, not 10: 12:05 pm is 12:05.)
The hour 11 is less than 12, so it is a morning time. Keep the hour and write am: 11:10 am.
12 is the hour just after midday, so it is pm. Do not take away 12. 12:25 is 12:25 pm.
00 is the hour just after midnight. In 12-hour time we call it 12 am. 00:55 is 12:55 am.

items.q: Ishaan’s train leaves at 17:52. What is this in 12-hour time?
items.e: 17 is more than 12, so it is pm. 17 − 12 = 5. 17:52 is 5:52 pm. (Dropping the 1 gives 7:52 pm, which is 19:52.)
Hours 13 to 23 are pm. Take away 12: 19 − 12 = 7. So 19:56 is 7:56 pm. (Do not just drop the 1: 9:56 pm is 21:56.)
Hours 13 to 23 are pm. Take away 12: 20 − 12 = 8. So 20:39 is 8:39 pm. (Take away 12, not 10: 10:39 pm is 22:39.)
Hours 13 to 23 are pm. Take away 12: 23 − 12 = 11. So 23:31 is 11:31 pm.
The hour 07 is less than 12, so it is a morning time: am. Drop the 0 at the front: 7:39 am.
The hour 10 is less than 12, so it is a morning time. Keep the hour and write am: 10:16 am.
12 is just after midday, so it is pm. Keep the 12: 12:04 pm.
00 is the first hour of the day, just after midnight. In 12-hour time it is 12 am: 12:16 am.

items.q: Which of these times is the latest in the day?
items.e: Change them all to 24-hour time: 9:15 pm = 21:15, 11:05 am = 11:05. 11:05, 18:30, 20:50, 21:15. The latest is 9:15 pm.

items.q: Which of these times is the earliest in the day?
items.e: Change them all to 24-hour time: 12:40 am = 00:40, 1:15 am = 01:15, 12:10 pm = 12:10. The day starts at 00:00, so the earliest is 12:40 am.
Hours 13 to 23 are pm. Take away 12: 15 − 12 = 3. So 15:20 is 3:20 pm. (Do not just drop the 1: 5:20 pm is 17:20.)
Hours 13 to 23 are pm. Take away 12: 13 − 12 = 1. So 13:55 is 1:55 pm. (Do not just drop the 1: 3:55 pm is 15:55.)
There are 60 seconds in 1 minute. (Not 100: time does not count in hundreds.)
A day is 24 hours: 12 a.m. hours and 12 p.m. hours. 12 + 12 = 24. (Not 12: the hour hand goes around the clock twice in one day.)

items.q: How many days are in a year that is not a leap year?
items.e: A year has 365 days. A leap year has one extra day, February 29, so it has 366. (52 is the number of weeks in a year. 360 uses 30 days in every month, but some months have 31.)
1 hour = 60 minutes. 4 × 60 = 240 minutes. (400 counts an hour as 100 minutes. 96 uses 24, but 24 is the hours in a day.)
1 minute = 60 seconds. 5 × 60 = 300 seconds. (500 counts a minute as 100 seconds. 65 adds 60 + 5 instead of multiplying.)
1 day = 24 hours. 3 × 24 = 72 hours. (36 uses 12 hours in a day. 180 uses 60.)
1 week = 7 days. 6 × 7 = 42 days. (30 counts only the 5 school days in each week. 13 adds 6 + 7.)

items.q: How many minutes are in three quarters of an hour?
items.e: A quarter of an hour is 60 ÷ 4 = 15 minutes. 3 × 15 = 45 minutes. (75 is three quarters of 100, but an hour is 60 minutes.)
1 year = 12 months. 2 × 12 = 24 months. (104 is the weeks in 2 years, and 730 is the days.)
3 hours = 3 × 60 = 180 minutes. 180 + 25 = 205 minutes. (325 counts an hour as 100 minutes. 145 counts only 2 hours.)
60 + 60 + 60 = 180 minutes make 3 hours. 210 − 180 = 30 minutes left. So 210 minutes = 3 hours 30 minutes. (2 hours 10 minutes counts an hour as 100 minutes.)
1 hour = 60 minutes and each minute = 60 seconds. 60 × 60 = 3,600 seconds. (6,000 uses 100 minutes in an hour. 120 adds 60 + 60.)
6 × 60 = 360 seconds make 6 minutes. 400 − 360 = 40 seconds left. So 400 seconds = 6 minutes 40 seconds. (4 minutes counts a minute as 100 seconds.)
1 week = 7 days and each day = 24 hours. 7 × 24 = 168 hours. (84 uses 12 hours in a day. 31 adds 7 + 24.)

items.q: Recess starts at 10:20 a.m. It lasts 25 minutes. What time does recess end?
items.e: Add 25 minutes: 10:45 a.m.

items.q: The school bus leaves at 8:35 a.m. The ride takes 40 minutes. What time does it get to school?
items.e: Add 40 minutes: 25 minutes takes you to 9:00 a.m., and 15 minutes more is 9:15 a.m.

items.q: Art class ends at 3:10 p.m. It lasted 35 minutes. What time did it start?
items.e: Count back 35 minutes: 10 minutes takes you to 3:00 p.m., and 25 minutes more is 2:35 p.m. (Count back to find a start time. Adding gives a time after 3:10 p.m.)

items.q: Gauri starts a science project at 1:45 p.m. and works for 50 minutes. What time does she stop?
items.e: Add 50 minutes: 15 minutes takes you to 2:00 p.m., and 35 minutes more is 2:35 p.m.

items.q: School starts at 8:45 a.m. Zoya’s bus ride takes 50 minutes. What time must she get on the bus?
items.e: Count back 50 minutes: 45 minutes takes you to 8:00 a.m., and 5 minutes more is 7:55 a.m. (Count back to find a start time. Adding gives a time after 8:45 a.m.)

items.q: Gym class starts at 11:25 a.m. It lasts 55 minutes. What time does it end?
items.e: Add 55 minutes: 35 minutes takes you to 12:00 noon, and 20 minutes more is 12:20 p.m. The time goes past 12 noon, so it changes from a.m. to p.m.

items.q: How long is it from 16:55 to 17:05?
items.e: Count on: 16:55 to 17:00 is 5 minutes, 17:00 to 17:05 is 5 minutes. 5 minutes + 5 minutes = 10 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: How long is it from 14:45 to 15:30?
items.e: Count on: 14:45 to 15:00 is 15 minutes, 15:00 to 15:30 is 30 minutes. 15 minutes + 30 minutes = 45 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: How long is it from 07:35 to 08:10?
items.e: Count on: 07:35 to 08:00 is 25 minutes, 08:00 to 08:10 is 10 minutes. 25 minutes + 10 minutes = 35 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: How long is it from 16:39 to 17:13?
items.e: Count on: 16:39 to 17:00 is 21 minutes, 17:00 to 17:13 is 13 minutes. 21 minutes + 13 minutes = 34 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: How long is it from 18:46 to 19:16?
items.e: Count on: 18:46 to 19:00 is 14 minutes, 19:00 to 19:16 is 16 minutes. 14 minutes + 16 minutes = 30 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: How long is it from 10:54 to 11:23?
items.e: Count on: 10:54 to 11:00 is 6 minutes, 11:00 to 11:23 is 23 minutes. 6 minutes + 23 minutes = 29 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: How long is it from 08:55 to 12:10?
items.e: Count on: 08:55 to 09:00 is 5 minutes, 09:00 to 12:00 is 3 hours, 12:00 to 12:10 is 10 minutes. 3 hours + 5 minutes + 10 minutes = 3 hours 15 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: How long is it from 10:50 to 13:15?
items.e: Count on: 10:50 to 11:00 is 10 minutes, 11:00 to 13:00 is 2 hours, 13:00 to 13:15 is 15 minutes. 2 hours + 10 minutes + 15 minutes = 2 hours 25 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: How long is it from 18:52 to 21:28?
items.e: Count on: 18:52 to 19:00 is 8 minutes, 19:00 to 21:00 is 2 hours, 21:00 to 21:28 is 28 minutes. 2 hours + 8 minutes + 28 minutes = 2 hours 36 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: How long is it from 09:26 to 11:09?
items.e: Count on: 09:26 to 10:00 is 34 minutes, 10:00 to 11:00 is 1 hour, 11:00 to 11:09 is 9 minutes. 1 hour + 34 minutes + 9 minutes = 1 hour 43 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: Recess starts at 10:15 a.m. and ends at 10:32 a.m. How long is recess?
items.e: Both times are in the same hour: 32 − 15 = 17 minutes.

items.q: Library time is from 1:05 p.m. to 1:48 p.m. How long is library time?
items.e: Both times are in the same hour: 48 − 5 = 43 minutes.

items.q: Music class is from 9:35 a.m. to 10:20 a.m. How long is music class?
items.e: Count on in jumps: 9:35 a.m. to 10:00 a.m. is 25 minutes; 10:00 a.m. to 10:20 a.m. is 20 minutes. 25 minutes + 20 minutes = 45 minutes. (Not 85 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the clock numbers.)

items.q: Gauri’s swimming lesson is from 4:50 p.m. to 5:35 p.m. How long is the lesson?
items.e: Count on in jumps: 4:50 p.m. to 5:00 p.m. is 10 minutes; 5:00 p.m. to 5:35 p.m. is 35 minutes. 10 minutes + 35 minutes = 45 minutes. (Not 85 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the clock numbers.)

items.q: Salmon cooks on the barbecue from 5:38 p.m. to 6:21 p.m. How long does it cook?
items.e: Count on in jumps: 5:38 p.m. to 6:00 p.m. is 22 minutes; 6:00 p.m. to 6:21 p.m. is 21 minutes. 22 minutes + 21 minutes = 43 minutes. (Not 83 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the clock numbers.)

items.q: Lunch is from 11:48 a.m. to 12:25 p.m. How long is lunch?
items.e: The time goes past 12 noon, from a.m. to p.m. Count on in jumps: 11:48 a.m. to 12:00 noon is 12 minutes; 12:00 noon to 12:25 p.m. is 25 minutes. 12 minutes + 25 minutes = 37 minutes. (Not 77 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the clock numbers.)

items.q: The Charity Run at school starts at 10:35 a.m. Vivaan finishes at 11:22 a.m. How long does he take?
items.e: Count on in jumps: 10:35 a.m. to 11:00 a.m. is 25 minutes; 11:00 a.m. to 11:22 a.m. is 22 minutes. 25 minutes + 22 minutes = 47 minutes. (Not 87 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the clock numbers.)

items.q: Harsh’s football practice is from 5:45 p.m. to 7:10 p.m. How long is practice?
items.e: Count on in jumps: 5:45 p.m. to 6:00 p.m. is 15 minutes; 6:00 p.m. to 7:00 p.m. is 1 hour; 7:00 p.m. to 7:10 p.m. is 10 minutes. 1 hour + 15 minutes + 10 minutes = 1 hour 25 minutes. (Not 1 hour 65 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the clock numbers.)

items.q: A movie starts at 6:55 p.m. and ends at 9:10 p.m. How long is the movie?
items.e: Count on in jumps: 6:55 p.m. to 7:00 p.m. is 5 minutes; 7:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. is 2 hours; 9:00 p.m. to 9:10 p.m. is 10 minutes. 2 hours + 5 minutes + 10 minutes = 2 hours 15 minutes. (Not 2 hours 55 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the clock numbers.)

items.q: A kabaddi game is from 6:40 p.m. to 8:55 p.m. How long is the game?
items.e: Count on in jumps: 6:40 p.m. to 7:00 p.m. is 20 minutes; 7:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m. is 1 hour; 8:00 p.m. to 8:55 p.m. is 55 minutes. 1 hour + 20 minutes + 55 minutes = 2 hours 15 minutes. (20 minutes + 55 minutes = 75 minutes = 1 hour 15 minutes.)
